pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as three to four sessions of 30-45 minutes plus daily mobility, with a specific promise aimed at his injury: 'your hip is going to get better, so you're going to be able to squat if you want to do that again.' He answered 'Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah' with no questions. Agreed without probing — though he had already sold himself on the modality before the call, having watched Trevor for two weeks and trained with kettlebells for a week and a half.

Framed as small tweaks rather than change, and correctly so — he had already cut from three or four meals to two and skips breakfast. The rep tied it to Trevor's own intermittent fasting and confirmed the occasional brownie is fine. Response was 'Yeah, 100%.' No questions. Notably he had earlier connected food directly to his ADHD brain fog — 'if I eat bad, I'm going to be all foggy' — and that thread was not picked up when the nutrition pillar was delivered.

Unambiguously the pillar he bought, and the most emotionally loaded reaction in the batch. Asked which of the three would help most he chose it immediately: 'Probably just holding me accountable... not that I'm lazy, because I love going to the gym. It's just knowing that somebody's better than me is holding me accountable. I gotta make him happy. I want him to see me succeed.' Then he went further, unprompted: 'I'm gonna look at him like he's my dad. I can't make my dad sad. I gotta keep him happy... dad, I'm not gonna fail you, I promise.' He had also framed it earlier through his Army background — a drill sergeant telling him what to do, 'yes, sir, I'll do it'. This is precisely why the community downsell failed: the product he wanted was the person.

anchors.raw: I had a coach before, like a workout coach, and the highest, was like $200 a month.
anchors.note: The decisive anchor. He has bought coaching before and knows what he paid for it — $200 a month, which is $1,200 for six months against a $6,000 offer. Volunteered in the same breath as 'I can't do it, man', so the comparison is doing the refusing. Note it also happens to be exactly the price of the community tier the rep then offered, which is why that number registered as reasonable to him even though the product did not.

anchors.raw: I'd probably do like $150 a month
anchors.note: His own stated monthly capacity, offered as a rough estimate pending actual budgeting, and pushed by the rep toward $200. Against $1,000/month for the one-to-one, the gap is roughly seven-fold. He is not currently earning and is about to take a job specifically to create room.

anchors.raw: I got kids and like if I was just like if I was just me and I just had my own thing going on, then yeah. But I have a wife and like five kids. Like, you know what I mean? Like, it's just a lot.
anchors.note: Five children on a single disability income, with a ring-fenced emergency fund he stated twice he would not touch: 'What I have set aside is just for my family emergency. Not like my personal.' Any money for this has to come from a job he has not started yet.

anchors.raw: I'd be at the gym and I'll have this, like, video up, and I'd be, like, trying to mimic him, you know what I mean? And I just try to do exactly what he does and just get the form correctly.
anchors.note: He is already running the programme for free by copying the videos at the gym, and it is working — 'even like in this week and a half of me just doing this, I can see my cuts coming back in.' The free version is producing visible results before any money changes hands, which is the hardest possible starting position. The one thing it does not give him is form correction, which he named himself ('my form is not bad, it's just I try to figure out how do I do this'), and that gap was never converted into value.

anchors.raw: my wife, like, at the same time, my wife is the same mode. She's like, we have to go, like, we're gonna go to the gym... And she looks good, so I have to look good, too.
anchors.note: He already has a fit, motivated training partner at home who drags him to the gym — free accountability, which is the exact pillar he said he most needs to buy. The rep never addressed why paid accountability adds something his wife does not, and this is arguably why the accountability sale, despite landing emotionally, did not convert.

anchors.raw: I wanted to get one-on-one coaching too, but I had way too little money at that point... he also told me, you can want to do one-on-one, but if you can't, then you have to go for a second best thing
anchors.note: An anchor the rep created about himself. Told well and honestly, and it built real rapport — but it also establishes that the person selling the $6,000 tier did not buy it, started on the cheap one, and got results anyway. As social proof for the downsell it works; as support for the premium it does the opposite.

unmet_demand.want: Direct one-to-one contact with Trevor at a price near $150-200 a month
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The ladder jumps from a $200/month peer community with no personal access to $6,000 for the one-to-one, with nothing in between. He rejected the substitute on exactly the dimension that matters to him — 'I would just want to talk to the man myself' — having already identified personal accountability as the single thing he needs. This is a genuine hole in the product ladder for a buyer who wants the premium ingredient in a smaller dose.

unmet_demand.want: Rehabilitation of a service-connected hip injury that currently prevents him squatting
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The injury was disclosed and lightly probed, then a direct therapeutic claim was made in the presentation — 'your hip is going to get better, so you're going to be able to squat if you want to do that again' — with no severity assessment, no duration question, no knowledge of what the injury actually is, and no awareness of what he is on disability for. He is a veteran with a documented accident injury and no clinician was mentioned by either side.

unmet_demand.want: Training and nutrition that account for ADHD and the brain fog he links to food
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He raised ADHD unprompted, connected it explicitly to diet, and said it is part of why he identifies with Trevor, who has spoken about having it. The rep acknowledged it in one garbled aside and never returned to it — not in the nutrition pillar, not in the accountability pillar, where structure and external prompting are precisely the ADHD-relevant selling points. A missed positioning opportunity rather than a product limitation.

unmet_demand.want: Form correction on the kettlebell movements he is currently self-teaching from video
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is arguably served — video form review is in both tiers, and the rep confirmed the community tier includes it. It is listed because he named the need clearly and it was never used as the argument against the free substitute he is currently relying on, which is the one place it would have done real work.
